title: Music at home and his parents' lessons
summary: His mother sight-read piano and his father directed church choirs; Jones recalls the discipline they taught him and gives his parents' names.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Was there music in your home? I mean did anybody play?
Oh, yes, my mother played piano. She
could sight read on piano. And my father, oh, yeah, he did a lot of choir directing around Chicago in those days, you know?
Did he do any choir directing in Memphis, or was it when he got to Chicago?
No, both places, you know. And then --
Where? Do you remember the names of the churches, or was it churches that he directed?
Yeah, church choirs. One was -- oh, it was a Congregational church. We called it Good Shepherd. A beautiful church, you know.
Was that Chicago?

Uh-huh. Now, before then I just didn't -- I knew that he had done this, because my family -- the other part of my family in Memphis had told me all about that. And then I began to do research on my father, because he just never said. You know, just took everything for granted. And of course my mother was a great support to him. We had our ups and downs and whatever, but it all turned out quite well. I really appreciate -- oh, how can I say this -- the things that they told me when I was in my early teens still work today.
What kind of things?
Oh, like you're disciplined with yourself. Your desire to do something worthwhile, no matter what's going on. Just stay on top of your own case, keep
going. And I just wish they could -- they really laid the foundation for me. I wish they could have been around now to see that it has turned out pretty good.
Uh-huh.

That's the only regret I have, now, you know, the ones that laid the foundation are not here. You know? But if I want to fantasize I might say that they saw something that in the future, you know, they saw something. But they were able to guide me right.
Your father was James Henry Jones, Sr.
Senior, yeah.
Your mother's name was what?
Mary -- well, I'll give you her maiden name.
All right.
Mary Genevra Young.
How do you spell Genevra?
Well, let me see. I've got to think about that, do it phonetically. G-e-n-e-v-r-a.
Just the way it sounds.
Yeah. Just phonetically, you know. So --
